transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

It is very unlikely to be faulty because heat pump dryers are designed to run cooler and take longer than your old condenser model, so what you are describing sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault. The lower temperature saves energy but means the cycle will naturally be closer to three hours for heavy items like towels. To rule out simple issues that can slow drying down, please check two things: first, ensure the lint filter in the door frame is completely clean and free of fluff, as this restricts airflow; second, verify you are not using a 'cool air' or delicate programme which uses little to no heat.

Ok well I clean the fluff filters after every single load, so that's not it. And I use Cotton Cupboard Dry with the drum full, so not a cool or delicate setting. It does get the clothes dry in the end, just takes ages.

Since you have already cleaned the lint filter and confirmed the programme is correct, we need to look at the specific design of your machine to see if there are model-specific quirks or potential blockages. Could you please provide the make and model number? This information is usually found on a sticker inside the door opening. If you cannot reach that label right now, don't worry about it for this step.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Bosch, model WTH85223GB, I've got it from the receipt. I don't need a replacement though, I just want to know why it takes so long!

The reason your towels take nearly three and a half hours is because heat pump dryers are designed to run at lower temperatures than condenser models, which makes them much more energy-efficient but significantly slower. The "Cotton Cupboard Dry" programme on the Bosch WTH85223GB is an eco-friendly cycle that uses very low heat for a long time to save electricity, so feeling barely warm in the first half hour is actually normal behaviour for this specific setting. Since you have already cleaned the lint filter after every load and confirmed the machine eventually gets the towels dry, there are no signs of a fault or blockage. You can switch to a standard "Cottons" programme if you need them dry faster, though it will use more energy than your current eco-setting.
